A.biggest_strength: Consistent stream color-coding that pedagogically links sequence numbers, acknowledgment numbers, and byte consumption (SYN in green, FIN in red, payload bytes) across the diagram, top equations, and inspector panel.
A.biggest_weakness: Relies on three curated ISN presets rather than permitting free-form student input for arbitrary ISN or payload numbers.

B.biggest_strength: Interactive input fields that allow students to enter custom initial sequence numbers and payload lengths, with instant recalculation of all sequence and acknowledgment fields.
B.biggest_weakness: Missing standard viewport meta tag and hard minimum SVG width that cause mobile browsers to render the page as a tiny, zoomed-out desktop layout unusable on phones.

structured_output.reasons: Page A is a masterclass in technical explanation and visual design. Its color-coded stream tracking (client bytes/server ACKs in blue, server bytes/client ACKs in gold, SYN in green, FIN in red) immediately illuminates the core logic of TCP sequence and acknowledgment numbers. It also provides real-time TCB state variables (SND.NXT and RCV.NXT), dual-level navigation (scenes and step slider), verification against real Linux tcpdump captures, and a responsive mobile layout that reflows the SVG into a vertical stack. In contrast, while Page B offers good interactive inputs and accurate calculations, it lacks directional stream color-coordination and suffers from a major mobile failure due to omitting the viewport meta tag.
